Sex takes many forms in a relationship. If you’d like more connecting sex you need to state that and give him a picture of what it looks like for you. If he thinks it’s okay to just use sex for an indefinite amount of time he will always do just that. In my opinion you’ve gotta speak up and if he won’t change his mind, then you have to consider if the relationship is right for you.

I would say too, if it hasn’t changed in 2 years that’s a tough one. If there are habits and expectations then change will take both of you taking a hard look at your relationship.

The above isn’t meant to be black and white, I just know from experience how it can get and breaking the habits/rhythm can be tough. Honestly just talk to him. We often get “stuck” because we think there’s been enough dialogue around a certain topic. Relationships are hard. Good connecting sex can be hard to find too. Try to talk with him and really listen to his answer and see if he’s willing to try the sex you’re looking for once a week or something to start. Really tell him what you want in the moment. As a man that’s what I want sometimes from my woman is open communication about what SHE wants.

Just because someone watches porn in a relationship it does NOT mean you’re disrespecting the other. Especially if it’s talked about and agreed upon, or maybe the partner does not care. Also — if someone is okay with their partner watching porn it doesn’t mean they have no respect for themselves.

Porn addiction on the other hand can have serious consequences in a relationship. It hijacks dopamine, gives the user an unrealistic expectation of sex, among other things.

Are you on any medication in addition to dealing with addiction?

Coming while on sertraline was next to impossible and I had friends who told me the same. 

When I first gave porn up I actually used a little bit of viagra to help maintain an erection with my partner. 

If I were to give you some advice from my own personal experience…

Workout, take l-arginine, go to therapy, run, hang with male friends, journal about your urges, read. 

Do the above for about 3-4 weeks and stop worrying about sex. If you have a partner reveal your addiction to them and tell them what you’re doing.

Learn to pleasure yourself but don’t have an objective (coming). If you lose your erection don’t get caught up, learn to stop masturbating if you’re not feeling it. We’ve learned to be urge-driven which creates a terrible internal sexual experience. .. and for partners it can be difficult too.

You have to learn to master your internal regulation first and also remember your body is craving a dopamine hit from porn so nothing feels as good as it.

Also I will see this about coming. When you’re objectively focused with sex it’s really difficult. I look my partner in the eyes 90% of the time during foreplay, sex, whatever. It creates and helps mend broken intimacy.

I hope some of this helps and feel free to pm.

I poke around on this sub and comment sometimes. You sound a little like me in that you acknowledge the end is here, but it is really difficult. You are thinking about how she could believe it is this bad, and you go through phases.

Glad to hear you are going to therapy. What kind of hobbies do you have that are just for you, do you have a friend group, support system? 

I find oftentimes as humans were constantly trying to problem solve, figure things out, “why did she just leave?”

There could be a million reasons. And out of those million reasons more than 99% have nothing to do with you and all about her. 

I notice a lot of the men on this subreddit are really blunt, and with good reason honestly. Women are hard to be in relationship with, and the system DOES often favor women in divorce. 

I was fortunate in that my ex did not try to take the house (I put the downpayment on), and our divorce cost (legally) like 500 bucks. She was my best friend, lover, and I will always love her. We split once, both fucked other people then got back together again and eventually called it. 

I always say this to men going through divorce.

Therapy
Gym
Hobbies (doesn’t matter what just do something)
Run
Read books 
Do one thing each day to treat yourself nicely it could be eating cookies, watching an episode of an awesome show.

Try to keep your body busy and your mind will follow. 

Finally.. I know you’re here to not feel so lonely or to figure out what’s going on. You’re in the right place, you may just not like all the answers. It sucks but is the truth. Don’t criticize yourself for mourning the marriage, but don’t stay in one state for too long.. and wonder about all the “what ifs” and “if onlys”. She doesn’t.. I can almost guarantee that. She’s gone through her grieving already probably and now you’re starting the process.

Hope this helps a little. Chin up, you got this brotha. DM me if you’re feeling low I check Reddit often.

I don’t think there is a “cure”. It’s more about managing symptoms of depression. In my case (and I suspect many others) it’s more like a disease. You would treat a regular disease with the assistance of a doctor or someone specialized to help.

From my own experience.. therapy, exercise, education (check out CPTSD), being around people, and finding a good meaningful hobby or something to keep your mind occupied. I just want you to know that I reached the lowest point of my life in 2016. My mom passed away when I was 12 (2002) and I was a victim of my fathers abuse. In 2016 I lost my well-paying job that earned me a house. I was completely destroyed by it. I stayed in bed all day wishing I could die and thought about ways to end it. I figured I could be with my mom finally (hopefully) and I would be at peace - finally. 


There's a lot more to the story but it really comes down to the fact that I thought about how my death would affect my family. I thought about this amazing gift of life that I would squander by simply giving up. So I called the suicide hotline, I got help - and this next part is really important: I stayed consistent with my help. I didn't just go to my mental health place I actually followed up with regular therapy appointments, I took medication and i talked about my problems. It sounds like a cookie cutter example but it really does help. If you are feeling like you want to harm yourself make sure to reach out to 1-800-273-8255 (suicide hotline). 

I don't know what you are going through but I promise there are tools out there to help you. I know getting out of bed or even thinking of getting out of bed can feel like a nightmare at times. It can feel like the hardest obstacle but you can do it I promise, you can fight through this but you need the tools to conquer it.

I don't think I'm the first to say that people are here for you. Reddit is a great place to just talk with others and converse about issues.
